---
title: "Before you arrive"
subtitle: "Do this before Monday 21 September"
---

**Time:** about 4 hours in total. Spread it over several evenings.
**Before you start:** the laptop you will bring to IISc.
**When you finish:** your laptop runs R, you have already written R code and
computed a risk ratio, and you have read one paper closely.

## Do these 5 steps, in this order

| | Step | Time | Go here |
|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | 1. Install R, RStudio and Quarto | 30 min | [Step 1](install.qmd) |
| ☐ | 2. Install the packages and run the check | 20 min | [Step 2](check-setup.qmd) |
| ☐ | 3. Send us your check result | 2 min | [Step 3](send-result.qmd) |
| ☐ | 4. Do the 9 browser primers | 2 h 45 min | [Step 4](primers.qmd) |
| ☐ | 5. Do the reading | 25 min | [Step 5](pre-reading.qmd) |

Do Step 1 first.

## If you are short of time

Do them in this order. Stop when you run out of evening.

1. **Steps 1, 2 and 3.** Without these you cannot do the hands-on work at all.
2. **Epidemiology primers 6 to 9.** These carry the concepts the lectures build
   on. Start with Primer 9, on bias and confounding.
3. **R primers 1 to 5.** We re-teach the basics in the room, so these can wait.
4. **Step 5,** the reading. 25 minutes. Do it on the train.

## Open the primers at home, not at IISc

The primers run R inside your web browser. The first page you open downloads
about 17 MB. The heaviest page downloads about 37 MB. Your browser keeps that
download for 7 days.

**You should see:** a page you opened at home this week loading in a few seconds
when you open it again at IISc.

**If it does not work:** open the primers before you travel. If 40 people
download 37 MB at the same moment on Monday morning, the venue wifi will not
cope.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
5 days is a short time. If your laptop is not ready on Monday morning, you will
spend the first session watching downloads instead of working. We cannot give
that time back.

Step 1 is first because it is the only step that can fail on the day, and the
only one we cannot fix for you in the room.

Step 4 is the long one. The 9 primers teach the R and the epidemiological
arithmetic that every hands-on block assumes you already have. Participants who
skip them spend the first sessions catching up.
:::

## Stuck?

1. Read [Troubleshooting](../resources/troubleshooting.qmd). It covers the
   common install failures on Windows, macOS and Linux.
2. If that does not help, email
   [office.msicph@iisc.ac.in](mailto:office.msicph@iisc.ac.in).
3. Include 3 things: your operating system and its version, the exact error
   message, and the output of `sessionInfo()`.

Do not wait until the weekend before the course to ask. We answer email on
working days.
